$texture.$comment: v0.9.2 (FEEDBACK §5.3 — Amith's anti-smoothness ask, enforceable): the means must be right AND organically noisy, or the data reads as generated to exactly the knowledgeable prospect it's calibrated for. All noise is SEEDED (deterministic — same seed, same wobble). Amplitudes below are ESTIMATES to be finalized in the ruleset spec, CO-DESIGNED with the mean tolerances (noise sized independently of tolerances randomly fails builds) and with the pilot's effect-size bands (noise must not wash out the causal signal).

requirements.name: renewal_yoy_band
requirements.metric: yearly renewal rate wanders within a band around the 87% mean
requirements.target: [0.84, 0.90] with year-over-year variance ABOVE a floor (anti-smoothness assertion)
requirements.source: calibrated to real YoY jitter in the verified 990 dues trends (size-twin deltas: -3.9, -4.8, -1.0, -3.6, -4.8 %/yr — real data is lumpy)

requirements.name: monthly_activity_autocorrelation
requirements.metric: registrations/sends/tickets carry autocorrelated month-to-month wobble (not iid noise, not flat)
requirements.target: positive lag-1 autocorrelation on monthly deltas, on top of seasonal cycles
requirements.source: ESTIMATE — shape requirement; amplitude in ruleset spec

requirements.name: distribution_lumpiness
requirements.metric: money distributions (gifts, spend, order sizes) are mixtures, not clean unimodal shapes
requirements.target: multi-component mixtures per the existing gift/payment models; no perfectly round counts
requirements.source: FEP gift shape + Atradius/CRF payment mixtures already imply this — generalized as a default

requirements.name: timestamp_texture
requirements.metric: operational timestamps carry day-of-week and holiday texture
requirements.target: weekday-skewed office actions, weekend-skewed member browsing, holiday dips

requirements.name: variance_floors_in_checks
requirements.metric: the benchmark validation itself asserts MINIMUM variance per headline metric (suspicious smoothness fails the build, same as a missed mean)
requirements.target: per-metric floors defined in the ruleset spec's validation harness
requirements.source: FEEDBACK §5.3 — enforce roughness both directions or it erodes as people tune toward targets

scalingLaws.$comment: primaryMagnitude = member count. Derived cardinalities preserve ratios across small(500)/medium(2500)/large(15000 — CANONICAL, v0.8; cheese-domain.md's 10,000 aligned). Sources: R3 §3 + R2 volume anchors. REV 2026-07-02: org count re-based — v1's 40 orgs (and the v2 plan's ~25 at medium) cannot support the ACS-calibrated competition chain (1,600 entries ÷ 7.5 per company needs ~210 entrant companies). DEVIATION FROM v2 PLAN — flag in Marcelo reconciliation. ⚠ v0.8 KNOWN LIMIT (GAP-5): these laws are calibrated at 2,500 and mostly LINEAR — they do NOT hold at 15,000 (35% conference attendance × 15k ≈ 5,250 attendees; no craft-food society looks like that). Large preset needs size-dependent attenuation exponents (participation rates fall with org size) before it is generated — see ../gaps-to-fill.md GAP-5.

derived.law: members * 0.25 (~625 at medium; avg ~4 affiliated members/org, mostly small creameries/retailers; some members unaffiliated). DERIVATION CHAIN (v0.9.2, so this isn't re-litigated): the anchor is ACS's REAL 211 entrant companies (verified) → entrant_orgs ≈ 210 → ÷0.75 entry-participation (ESTIMATE) → producer_orgs ≈ 280 → ÷0.45 producer share (R2-consistent ESTIMATE) → orgs ≈ 625 → ratio 0.25 is the RESULT of that chain, not an independent fact
organizations * 0.45 (~280 at medium; consistent with ~1,000 US artisan producers, R2)
producer_organizations * 0.75 (~210 at medium — matches ACS 2025: 211 companies)
6 + members^0.5 * 0.18 (~15 at medium — R3 recommended 10-15; v1 had ~4)
2.2 (deliberate 2x scale-up over v1's actual ~1.0-1.1/member/yr [R3 §3] so engagement analytics have substance; conference alone contributes ~0.58)

sizeAttenuation.$comment: GAP-5 FILLED 2026-07-06 — sources APPROVED (Marcelo: real-association sources acceptable; point selection delegated; relevance-weighted). FIT POINTS (member-conference orgs only, relevance order): American Culinary Federation 14,000 members → ~9-14% convention attendance (HIGHEST weight — food-craft domain, right size band); School Nutrition Assn 50,000 → ~12.5%; Academy of Nutrition & Dietetics 112,000 → ~9%; anchor ACS 2,300 → 35%. EXCLUDED from fit: IFT + SCA (trade expos — attendance ≥ membership, different mechanism), ASA (joint-meeting confound), AIHA (non-member inflation) — the last two sit ABOVE the fitted curve and bracket it from above. Full citations: research/candidate-sources/gap5-size-attenuation-sources.md. ⚠ DATA POINTS ONLY — no subject matter from these orgs enters the demo (Marcelo's standing constraint).

participation_alpha.law: participation-type rates scale as rate(N) = rate(2500) * (N/2500)^(alpha-1) with alpha = 0.55 +/- 0.10
participation_alpha.note: REVISED 2026-07-06 per Marcelo: alpha NO LONGER applies to the flagship conference — conference size at large uses REAL reported turnouts (below). Alpha retained only for non-conference participation rates. Fit basis: ACF ~0.35-0.4, SNA/AND ~0.65-0.67

conference_attendance_large.target: flagship total registrants 2,000 +/- 500 at 15,000 members; member attendees ~1,400 +/- 400 (~9% +/- 3), non-member share ~30% holds
conference_attendance_large.note: REVISED 2026-07-06 (Marcelo: 'don't use scaling for conferences — use real reported turnouts of similar-size orgs'). REAL DATA BASIS: ACF 14k members → convention ~1,200-2,000 (cafemeetingplace.com 2017 official; 2026 claim); American Translators Assn 8.5k members → annual conference ~1,100-1,300 (atanet.org + ata63.org, 2023-25); bracketed above by ACDA 22k → '~10k' reported but heavily inflated by honor-choir performers/families (10times.com — low quality, weight near zero) and SNA 50k → 6-6.5k. Medium keeps the ACS-derived 0.35. Citations: research/candidate-sources/gap5-size-attenuation-sources.md. $v091 VERIFICATION: ATA 1,300 (2023) and ACF 1,200+ (2017) re-confirmed against sources; the ~2,000 upper anchor rests on weak 2026 sources (Instagram + an unvetted estimator) — treat the 2,000 central value as an UPPER-MID estimate; the tolerance already covers the honest range

sizeAttenuation.conference_structure_at_scale: REAL-WORLD PATTERN (NSTA, ~35-40k members): large societies run MULTIPLE conferences per year (NSTA runs 2 nationals/yr — $v091 correction: its AREA conferences were discontinued in 2019, replaced by the second national; remaining events are web seminars/institutes) — the two-nationals pattern still validates the multi-event portfolio for the large preset rather than one giant flagship
sizeAttenuation.event_portfolio_at_large: total events/yr still grows (the events_per_year sqrt law holds; regional conferences + workshops multiply) — the FLAGSHIP's member-share falls per the alpha law while the regional portfolio absorbs participation; net event_registrations_per_member_year at large ~1.6-1.8 (down from 2.2 at medium)

revenue_at_large.note: ACF — a real 14k-member food-craft org — books $3.81M (FY2024 990): revenue per member FALLS with size (~$680 @2.5k → ~$270 @14k). Large preset total revenue ~$4M, NOT 6x the medium $1.7M

governance_at_large.note: committees / seats / volunteer share at 15k — ESTIMATE (alpha~0.2: governance grows far slower than membership; ASAE median 8 committees is size-insensitive in the survey). Hardening via full 990 XML pulls is DEMO-BACKLOG BL-4
